correctness.rationale: Every square-zero dual-number matrix A+εB satisfies A²=0 and AB+BA=0. In a Jordan basis of square-zero A of rank r, an invertible sign operator P anti-commutes with A in every characteristic and maps B to BP, so the tangent fiber is a centralizer of dimension (n-r)²+r². Counting image, kernel and induced isomorphism of A gives [n r]_q[n-r r]_q|GL_r|; the q-exponents sum exactly to n², proving the displayed product. Finite-product estimates yield the uniform O_q(1) total-weight error and uniform O_q(1/n) CDF bound. The standalone finite verifier independently checks all reduced A, ranks, tangent linear kernels and, for several cases, all B, including a GF4 prime-power example. Infinite cases rely on the written proof, not enumeration.

originality.rationale: The full claim (all-rank first-jet census plus O(1/n) uniform-rank law) was compared by actual searches against the closest accessible primary statements, published research summaries and own historic claims. The Cheong et al. hypothesis square-free modulo p excludes t²; Prasad et al. concern similarity orbits, not these labeled square-zero rank weights; D'Alesio gives the scheme but not the finite-field jet enumeration. Indexed same-ring results count strongly nil-clean matrices or nilpotency-index profiles of a single Jordan block. No inspected theorem implies the joint count and rank law. Priority remains provisional, especially against a general jet-scheme result.

value.rationale: The square-zero scheme is a natural singular representation variety; counting its first-order points by reduction rank is motivated by nilpotent matrix polynomial equations over length-two coefficient rings. The exact all-n rank strata reveal a surprising macroscopic uniform rank law where field-level square-zero matrices concentrate at the maximum feasible rank. This is a natural complete invariant and a qualitative asymptotic phase change, not an arbitrary parameter slice, a restatement of a single known count, or a mere finite experiment.
